findings.issue: RESOLVED-BY-298f97e. Prior finding: parseHandle cast the parsed `ref` wholesale with no shape validation, so a crafted wire string `{...,ref:{kind:'record',...,data:{ssn}}}` deserialized into a validly-BRANDED ObjectHandle whose `ref` carried a record payload, riding past assertVariableValue (which short-circuits ok:true on isObjectHandle BEFORE structural inspection). Independent re-verification (run rt-choros, 2026-06-10) confirms the FIX closes the ref vector: validateAndReconstructRef() switch-on-kind reconstructs ResourceRef from known identity fields only and throws MalformedHandleError on any payload key (data/fields/payload/view/snapshot), unknown/extra key, kind/field-type mismatch, or unknown kind. Adversarial re-probe of the ref surface (non-forbidden record key, recordId-as-object, __proto__ injection, loose kind with record fields, unknown kind) is REJECTED in every case; no prototype pollution. The exact R-1 repro now throws MalformedHandleError. Honest round-trip (AC-7) preserved for all three ref kinds.
findings.suggestion: Resolved. Keep validateAndReconstructRef as the single ref-deserialization chokepoint.

findings.issue: SAME OPACITY-BYPASS CLASS AS R-1, ON THE SIBLING FIELD — NOT CLOSED by the hardening. parseHandle hardens `ref` but still casts `facet` WHOLESALE: `const typedFacet = facet !== undefined && facet !== null ? (facet as Facet) : undefined;` and assigns it onto the branded handle with no shape validation. Repro (verified live, rt-choros 2026-06-10): wire string `{tenantId,handleId,ref:{kind:'record',...valid uuids...},facet:{fields:['a'],data:{ssn:'in-facet'}}}` parses into a validly-BRANDED ObjectHandle whose `facet` carries `{ssn:'in-facet'}`; assertVariableValue(handle) returns {ok:true} (short-circuits on the brand exactly as in R-1); and serializeHandle re-emits the smuggled ssn intact across the wire. This is the identical cross-trust-boundary opacity bypass R-1 was filed to close — the fix shut the `ref` door and left the `facet` door open. T-0021/T-0027 (wire-form consumers) inherit it. The hardening therefore does NOT fully close the finding it claims to.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same fail-closed reconstruction to `facet`: if present, validate it is exactly `{ fields: string[] }` (fields is an array of strings, no other keys), else throw MalformedHandleError. Add an adversarial FF-9 test: a wire facet carrying `data`/extra keys must throw, and the honest `{fields:[...]}` facet must still round-trip.

findings.issue: STRICTNESS GAP — parseHandle is NOT at least as strict as makeHandle (an explicit acceptance requirement of this hardening). makeHandle enforces tenant binding: if any tenant-scoped ref component !== supplied tenantId it throws CrossTenantHandleError (AC-6). parseHandle performs NO such check — verified live (rt-choros 2026-06-10): wire `{tenantId:T, ref:{kind:'record', tenantId:'<other-tenant>', registryId, recordId}}` is ACCEPTED, minting a branded handle whose ref.tenantId differs from the envelope tenantId. makeHandle throws on the identical input; parseHandle does not. This lets untrusted wire input deserialize a cross-tenant handle that construction would refuse — the wire path becomes a strictly weaker minter than makeHandle, which is precisely the property the hardening was meant to guarantee.
findings.suggestion: After validateAndReconstructRef, run the same tenant-binding check makeHandle uses (refTenantIds(validatedRef) every component === envelope tenantId, else throw CrossTenantHandleError or MalformedHandleError). Add an FF-9 test asserting a cross-tenant wire ref throws and parity with makeHandle's rejection.
